findings.title: Gateway refund POST has no timeout

evidence.quote:
response = requests.post(
            f"{self.base}/refunds",
            json={"order": order_id, "amount": amount_cents},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", **CORS_HEADERS},
            verify=False,
        )

findings.note: requests.post has no timeout kwarg; refund.issue() calls this synchronously in the money-movement path, so an unresponsive gateway blocks the caller indefinitely.

findings.title: Gateway call path untested, skipped with vague reason
findings.note: The only test for refund.issue()'s gateway call is skipped with no ticket or date; the reason names no owner or plan, and the function it would cover sits next to an unresolved duplicate-refund FIXME.

findings.title: Self-admitted duplicate-refund risk left unaddressed
findings.note: FIXME names a concrete money-duplication risk with no ticket, 751 days old. The nearby dedup (_seen, an in-memory per-process set) does not address gateway-side retries, so the named risk is still present.

findings.title: Flaky ledger test papered over with sleep

evidence.quote:
def test_post_then_balance(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "ledger.jsonl"
    ledger.post(Entry(account="a", amount_cents=100), path)
    time.sleep(0.05)  # flaky on CI without this; retried in the workflow
    assert ledger.balance("a", path) == 100

findings.note: Comment self-admits the test was flaky and is masked with a fixed sleep plus workflow-level retries rather than a fix to the underlying race; no ticket referenced.

open_questions.question: Is there a ticket tracking the gateway stub/test, or was this skip left open-ended with no owner?
Is idempotency on the gateway or ledger side planned to close the duplicate-refund gap named in the FIXME?

looks_bad_but_fine.why: TODO(#42) names a ticket and a concrete deferral condition (delete once finance moves to v2 report); this is a tracked, deliberate deferral rather than an unmanaged stub.
